learning_outcomes.text: A systematic understanding of the key concepts and aspects for the analysis and design of structures under dynamic loads.
Ability to apply knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate and solve calculation, design and testing problems for structures and their main systems using specifically established methods.
Ability to choose and apply relevant analytical and modeling methods in the calculation, design and testing of structures under dynamic loads.
Understand the different methods available for structural analysis and be able to use them.
Ability to design and perform experiments for the characterization of a structure under dynamic loads, as well as interpret data and draw conclusions.
Ability to combine theory and practice to solve structural engineering problems.
Understand the different applicable methods and techniques and their limitations for the analysis of structures under dynamic loads.
Awareness of the implications of engineering practice in the calculation of structures under dynamic loads.
Awareness of the responsibility of engineering practice, its social and environmental impact, and commitment to professional ethics, responsibility and standards of engineering practice.
A systematic understanding of the key concepts and aspects of their engineering branch.
An adequate knowledge of their engineering branch that includes some knowledge at the forefront of their field.
The ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate and solve engineering problems using established methods.
The ability to choose and apply relevant analytical and modeling methods.
Understanding of different methods and the ability to use them.
The ability to design and perform experiments, interpret data and draw conclusions.
The ability to combine theory and practice to solve engineering problems.
The understanding of applicable methods and techniques and their limitations.
Awareness of all implications of engineering practice.
Demonstrate awareness of the responsibility of engineering practice, its social and environmental impact, and commitment to professional ethics, responsibility and standards of engineering practice.

Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study based on general secondary education, and usually at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects involving knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competences usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and problem-solving within their field of study.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to design a system, component or process in the field of mechanical engineering, to meet the required specifications.
Knowledge and ability to apply current legislation as well as mandatory specifications, regulations and standards in the field of mechanical engineering.
Knowledge and ability to apply computational and experimental tools for the analysis and quantification of mechanical engineering problems.
Knowledge and ability for the calculation and design of structures and industrial constructions.

syllabus_topics: Review of free and forced oscillations
Presentation of the dynamic phenomenon and application of dynamic calculation to structures
Physical models and degrees of freedom
Free and forced oscillation in 1 DOF systems
Free and forced oscillation in 2 DOF systems
Free and forced oscillation in N DOF systems
Regulations relating to the seismic design of structures: design seismic actions
Application to the seismic design of structures (calculation examples)
Slender structures: cables, towers and posts

assessment_methods.method: Continuous Assessment (coursework, class participation, practicals, skill and knowledge tests)

assessment_rules: The final grade is based 100% on continuous assessment, which includes coursework, class participation, practicals, and skill and knowledge tests. Attendance and completion of scheduled laboratory practicals are mandatory to pass the course. In the extraordinary call, the final grade will be the maximum between (exam score including continuous assessment) and (exam score exclusively).
bibliography: Ray W. Clough, Joseph Penzien. Dynamics of structures. McGraw-Hill. 1993
